 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 10.03.2020 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and CJM and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
The Manager vs Mahesha R on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12518427/
2 Chamarajanagar in MVC No.313/2014 for having granted the compensation to the claimant by fixing the liability against the appellant-insurance company.
2.
Heard the arguments of the earned counsel for the appellant-insurance company and learned counsel for respondent No.1-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Respondent No.3 has remained absent and it has no liability in the offence.
3. The rank of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The case of the petitioner is that, on 21.01.2014 at about 1.30 p.m., when the petitioner was going to Chamarajanagar from Santhemarahalli village on his motorbike bearing registration No.KA10-Q-8413, the rider of the TVS XL NC: 2024:KHC:21392 Moped bearing No.KA-10-Q-7276 driven the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner from Chamarajanagar towards Santhemarahalli road and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was shifted to hospital and given treatment.

Therefore, claimed the compensation of Rs.19,10,000/-.
5.

In response to the notice, the owner of the vehicle TVS XL Moped (respondent No.1 before the Tribunal) filed statement of objection contending that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent on the part of the petitioner himself.
He denied the notional income of the injured and the injury sustained by the petitioner.
It is further contended that the petitioner himself driven the motor bike in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, it is contended that the owner of the vehicle is not liable to pay the compensation.

Hence,
prayed for dismissing the petition.

6. The insurer of TVS XL Moped No.KA-10-Q-7276 (respondent No.2 before the Tribunal), appeared and filed NC: 2024:KHC:21392 statement of objection contending that the owner has allowed a person to ride the said TVS XL moped and the said rider was not having the valid driving licence and therefore, the owner of the TVS XL Moped has violated the terms and condition of the insurance company.
Therefore, the respondent insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.

It is further contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the petitioner himself who was also having no driving licence and hence, contended that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

7. The insurer of the motorbike of the petitioner (Respondent No.3 before the Tribunal) also filed the statement of objections contending that the owner of the offending vehicle and the insurer of the offending vehicle were responsible for the said incident and therefore, the insurer of the offending vehicle are liable to pay compensation but, not the insurer of the motorbike of the petitioner and therefore, prayed for dismissing the petition.
Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues.

3 ISSUES 1.

Chamarajanagar-Santhemarahalli main road, on account of actionable negligence of the driver of the two wheeler namely TVS XL bearing reg. No.KA-10-Q-7276?

2. Whether the respondents prove that the accident had happened because of the negligent act of the petitioner himself as alleged in para 10 of the written statement of R2 and para No.4 of written statement of R1?
3. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or decree?

Whether the respondent No.2 proves that at the time of the accident the petitioner had no valid and effective driving licence?
9. The petitioner himself was examined as P.W.1 and got marked 19 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.19.
A doctor was examined as C.W.1 and got marked Exs.C.1 to C.3.

On behalf of respondents, the witnesses were examined as R.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.D.1, D.3.
10.
After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal answered issue Nos.1 and 3 in the affirmative and issue number 2 and the additional issue No.2 in the negative.

Accordingly, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.2,82,273/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation, by fixing the liability on respondent- insurance company of the TVS XL Moped No.KA-10-Q-7276.
Being aggrieved by the compensation awarded and fixing the liability on the insurance company of the offending vehicle, TVS XL Moped, the said insurance company is in this appeal.
Learned counsel for the appellant has seriously argued on two main grounds.
The first contention is that the rider of TVS XL Moped No.KA-10-Q-7276 was not having the valid and effective driving licence on the date of the accident.
Even the respond No.2-owner of said offending vehicle failed to appear before the Court and he did not produce driving licence in spite of the issue of notice as per Ex.D.2.
Therefore, it is a clear case that there was no licence for the rider of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, fixing liability on the appellant- insurance company is not correct.

In respect of his contention, he has relied upon the judgment of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in The Manager vs Mahesha R on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12518427/
4

sentences.text: The second limb of argument of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the compensation towards income an account of disability to the claimant does not arise as the claimant himself admitted in cross-examination that he is a businessman running business.

Therefore no loss would be accrued to the whole body and loss of income does not arise and hence,
prayed for reducing the compensation.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1- claimant has contended that the Tribunal has rightly considered the appeal.

The police have investigated the matter and the police could have filed charge sheet under Section 3 read with Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act and there is no driving licence for the rider of the offending vehicle i.e., TVS XL Moped.
Therefore, fixing the liability on the claimant - petitioner does not arise.

Even if this Court were to come to the conclusion that there is no liability to fix on the appellant- insurance company may direct the appellant-insurance company to pay and recover the same from the owner of the TVS XL moped vehicle.
It is further contended that the claimant being the businessman, has to pay attention and he is not properly concentrating on the business.

It is further contended even though the doctor has given disability to the limb, the Tribunal should have considered one third disability towards the whole body, which comes to 11%,
but the Tribunal has considered 6% towards whole body disability.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the quantum of compensation and hence, prayed for dismissing the appeal.
Learned counsel for the respondent N-.2-owner of the offered vehicle TVS XL moped has contended that there is no liability against him in the petition as well as in the appeal.
Respondent No.3-insurer of the claimant's vehicle is not represented.

14. Based upon the contentions of the learned counsel for the parties, the points that arise for consideration of this court:
(i) Whether the appellant is able to show that the rider of the offending vehicle TVS XL Moped No.KA-10-Q-7276 did not possess any valid driving licence ?
(ii) Whether the finding of the Tribunal answering against the appellant calls for interference?
(iii) Whether the compensation awarded by the tribunal requires to be reduced as it is excessive and exorbitant?
The Manager vs Mahesha R on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12518427/
5 15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On perusal of the records and the charge sheet material, it reveals that though the claimant rode the motorbike on the date of accident, but the rider of the TVS XL Moped,
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:21392 though it is a small vehicle, came in negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
The police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet material against the rider of TVS XL Moped and not against the petitioner, and there is no negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Exhibit P-8 clearly reveals that the accident was occurred in view of negligent riding of the TVS XL Moped.
16. The contention of the appellant is that the rider of TVS XL Moped had no driving license.
In respect of this case, PW-1 was examined.
It is the specific case of the respondent that there is no driving licence of the rider.
Even though on issuing notice, respondent No.1 - owner offending vehicle appeared before the court and filed statement of objection, but not entered witness box.

He also not taken any contention that the rider of the TVS XL Moped was having driving license or not produced any driving licence before the tribunal to show that the rider of the TVS XL Moped was having driving licence.

Such being the case, merely the police have not filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act, itself is not a ground to show the rider of the TVS - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:21392 XL Moped was having valid driving licence cannot be acceptable and

hence,
an adverse inference can be drawn against respondent No.2-owner that the rider of the moped does not have a valid driving licence on the date of the accident.
Therefore, in view of the absence of evidence on record, the Tribunal taking the view that the rider of TVS XL Moped was having driving licence, cannot be acceptable.
Therefore, the finding or the Tribunal on this aspect shall have to be set aside and it is to be held that the rider of TVS XL Moped was not having any valid licence at the time of accident.

17. In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Swarn singh reported in (2004)3 SCC 297 where it was held that the insurance company shall pay, in the first instance, with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in accordance with law.
The Hon'ble supreme court in the case of PAPPU AND OTHERS VS. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018)3 SCC 208, has also reiterated the same.

entities.text: PAPPU AND OTHERS VS. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018)3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the judgments of the Honorable Supreme Court, in the aforesaid cases, the liability has to be fixed on respondent no.2-owner.
Therefore, appellant - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:21392 insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from respondent no.2-owner.

The Manager vs Mahesha R on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12518427/
6 18.

entities.text: Manager vs Mahesha R on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In respect of quantum of compensation, the Tribunal has considered only 6% disability to the whole body.
Though the doctor has stated 33% disability to particular limb, but it was not for the whole body.

Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal assessed 18%
disability to the particular limb and 6% disability to the whole body.
Therefore, it does not require any interference in respect of loss of income due to disability.
There is no serious dispute by the appellant's counsel.
On the other hand, there is no need to look into the quantum of compensation.

19. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) Therefore, the appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The award of compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.2,82,273/- with interest at 6% per annum, from the date of petition till realisation, is affirmed.

(iii) The liability fixed on the appellant-insurer by the Tribunal is set aside and modified and directed the appellant being the insurer of the offending vehicle TVS XL moped is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner-claimant, and in turn, the appellant-insurer can recover the same from respondent No.2 herein (owner of the offending vehicle TVS XL Moped).
(iv) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
